text:
sre-oncall: FYI - seeing a sudden spike in 429s from edge-rate-limiter in us-west-2 starting ~15:33 PDT. Creating thread for timeline and mitigation. /cc @channel

ops-bot: [ALERT] edge-rate-limiter 429-rate > 5% (us-west-2)

danielle: Confirmed. Short-context generation routes and realtime streams are getting throttled. Tail latency also spiking for affected requests. Pulling limiter logs and recent config diffs.

owen: I pushed a change this morning to tighten per-tenant burst windows to reduce headroom on noisy tenants. Might be the trigger under today's traffic pattern.

platform-eng: Immediate mitigation options: 1) relax burst window, 2) enable soft-queueing in front of limiter, 3) route affected tenants to us-west-1. Applying 1 & 2 now to reduce customer impact.

marco: Customer impact: some Hosted customers and a handful of Dedicated tenants on us-west-2 observed 429s and stream disconnects. CS queue has 14 reports. No data loss reported.

ops-bot: [ACTION] env change applied: RATE_LIMIT_BURST_WINDOW=300ms -> 600ms at 15:38 PDT; soft_queue=true toggled. Rolling restart across edge pool initiated.

danielle: Logs (excerpt):
```
2026-09-12T15:34:01-07:00 WARN limiter: deny tenant=acme-corp key=gen-short err=burst_exceeded
2026-09-12T15:34:07-07:00 ERROR stream: connection closed status=429 tenant=acme-corp
2026-09-12T15:35:12-07:00 INFO config: RATE_LIMIT_BURST_WINDOW updated by owen
```

owen: After toggles, initial telemetry shows 429 rate drop from 5.2% -> 1.1% in 4 minutes. Some queues still backing up due to retries. Keeping routing fallback ready.

platform-eng: Routing fallback prep: we staged fallback routes to us-west-1 for flagged tenants; not enabled yet. Will flip if error rate not <0.5% in 15m.

cs: Drafting customer notification: "We experienced transient throttling in us-west-2 affecting short generation and streaming sessions. We've relaxed burst limits and enabled soft-queueing to reduce disruptions. We're monitoring and will follow up with an RCA."

ops-bot: [METRICS] Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/edge-rate/us-west-2?orgId=1 | Runbook: https://wiki.redwood.ai/runbooks/rate-limiter.md

marco: Preliminary root cause: overly aggressive burst tightening plus a traffic pattern spike (several customers replaying jobs) caused sudden exhaustion of per-tenant tokens. Recommendation: revert burst policy defaults and move noisy-tenant mitigation to out-of-band policing.

danielle: Commands used to relax config:
```
kubectl set env deployment/edge-rate-limiter RATE_LIMIT_BURST_WINDOW=600ms SOFT_QUEUE=true -n edge-us-west-2
kubectl rollout restart deployment/edge-rate-limiter -n edge-us-west-2
```

platform-eng: Current status: partially mitigated; 429 rate down to ~0.8% and falling. Monitoring for 30m. If stable we'll leave relaxed settings and plan policy change in config repo.

sre-oncall: ETA to normal (<0.5% 429s): 20-40 minutes if no additional traffic spikes. Postmortem owner: @owen - please lead RCA and remediation items.

owen: Acknowledged. I'll open the incident doc with timeline, config diffs, and action items. Target postmortem: 48 hours.

status-bot: [STATUS PAGE] Draft: https://status.redwood.infra/incidents/1799999999-preview (publishing in 15m)

cs: I'll queue the customer notice after ops sign-off. Will escalate any priority customers immediately.

sre-oncall: Thanks all. Keep updates brief here; escalate to PD if regressions occur. We'll close thread when 429 <0.5% for 15m and queue backlogs clear.
